newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Folgado says '96 public deficit on target.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Folgado says '96 public deficit on target.

text.p: Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said on Tuesday that the overall 1996 public sector deficit could be below the targeted 4.4 percent of gross domestic product, according to provisional data.
"..we can garantee the 4.4 percent target, it might even be lower," he said at a press conference.

Referring to Monday's fall in Spanish financial markets after negative remarks about the country's chances of entering European economic and monetary union (EMU) from its outset, Folgado said economic fundamentals would provide the key.
"What really matters is how economic and financial fundamentals are doing," Folgado said.
The Budget Secretary echoed recent comments by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar regarding the government's commitment to meeting EMU convergence targets.
He said EMU entry would depend on meeting the criteria per se, not on political statements.

"Entry in European monetary union will not depend on third party opinions but on the targets being met as written in the (Maastricht) Treaty...If these criteria are met, it doesn't matter what certain people say," he said.
Folgado said financial markets will reflect Spain's perceived fulfillment of Maastricht's convergence goals.

"We think that this year, as we'll approach important dates for the analysis of meeting the (convergence) objectives, (it) is logical that (there) are certain short-term movements on the financial markets", he said.
